dok_rationale: Part (c) coordinates both endpoints, two cutoffs, random-sample scope, and the mean-versus-individual distinction to adjudicate two interpretations and trace an advertising consequence.
stem: Suppose a library wants the mean setup time for all 800 kiosk transactions in a month below 45 seconds and hopes to advertise a mean below 42 seconds. An SRS of 25 has the shown summary. A 95\% one-sample $t$-interval is $(39.923,44.877)$ seconds.\par\smallskip \textbf{Mina:} ``I would compare each cutoff with the full interval and keep the conclusion about the population mean.''\par \textbf{Gabe:} ``Because the interval contains times below both cutoffs, I think it supports both claims; I also read 95\% as the share of transaction times inside it.''
first_take: Does the range 39.923 to 44.877 make both time claims believable? Give one reason.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Locate 42 and 45 relative to the interval.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Interpret the supplied 95\% interval in one sentence about the mean setup time for all 800 transactions.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: In 3--4 sentences, decide whose approach is justified. Use the interval to judge each cutoff, then explain what Gabe gets wrong about individual transaction times.

answers.a: The value 42 is inside $(39.923,44.877)$; 45 is above its upper endpoint.
answers.b: We are 95\% confident that the mean setup time for all 800 kiosk transactions that month is between 39.923 and 44.877 seconds.
answers.c: Mina is justified: the entire interval is below 45, supporting a population mean below 45 seconds. Because 42 is inside, means above 42 remain plausible, so a mean below 42 is not established. The interval estimates one population mean; it does not describe the middle 95\% of individual transaction times. The library should therefore avoid advertising a mean below 42 or a guarantee about individual times.

expectedElements.description: Uses the upper endpoint below 45 to support the mean-below-45 claim
Uses 42 inside the interval to reject support for the stronger claim
Explains that the interval estimates a mean rather than containing 95\% of transactions

scoringGuide.E: Uses both cutoff locations correctly and distinguishes the mean from individual transaction times.
scoringGuide.P: Shows substantive valid reasoning for at least one required element, but does not meet all E requirements. Credit correct reasoning even when another claim is wrong.
scoringGuide.I: Shows no substantive valid reasoning for any required element; a name, unsupported choice, or copied number alone does not count.
